How does GenGuard reduce GenAI data loss?

Trustity GenGuard is browser DLP: an extension plus Cloud Portal policy. It is designed to stop sensitive pastes into public GenAI chatbots, block risky domains, and surface Shadow IT / unsanctioned SaaS from the browser. Pasting source code into a public GenAI tool creates data-loss risk because sensitive code may leave the corporate boundary, vendor retention and training policies may be unclear, and this channel bypasses DLP that only watches email or USB. GenGuard keyword blocking, domain allow/block lists, and browsing categories are the product controls for that gap. Do not test with production-sensitive data.

How can a phone camera pointed at a screen cause data leakage even when USB and email DLP are enabled?

A phone camera pointed at a screen is a visual exfil channel. USB device control and email DLP never see the pixels. Photos can capture rendered secrets, PII, source, or customer data. Compensating controls: visual-channel detection (VisionX), workstation lock on policy, physical-area rules, and awareness. Digital egress tools remain necessary for files and paste; they do not close the camera path.

Does Axiom need a TAO agent on every device?

Trustity Axiom is edge SMB and DNS security: an inline SMB reverse proxy and policy-driven DNS nodes. It can run air-gap capable and does not require an endpoint agent on every device for this path, so it can cover IoT and BYOD that lack TAO. Policy-driven DNS at the edge reduces malware callback risk by blocking known-bad or DGA-like domains centrally. Axiom complements TAO endpoint controls; it is a portfolio product licensed separately from the Cloud Portal.

How should we harden a CEO Windows laptop for travel?

A minimal hardening checklist for a traveling executive Windows laptop: full-disk encryption; strong identity (SSO plus MFA, no standing local admin for daily work); patch cadence with auto-update; unique rotated local admin via PAM rather than a shared helpdesk password; disk/USB and browser DLP policies; screen lock and visual-channel controls for public spaces; VPN or Zero Trust access; inventory and HostGuard so stolen-device brute force is noisy. This is educational guidance, not a compliance certification.

What is the TAO agent?

Policy lives in the Trustity Cloud Portal. Enforcement happens on the endpoint and in the browser. The TAO agent is the Windows/Linux runtime for VisionX detection, PAM rotation, HostGuard IPS, browser DLP hooks, and asset inventory. Trustity does not push the installer from the cloud; IT downloads Setup from Deployment and distributes it (Intune, SCCM, GPO, or controlled install) using the organization license key. Agents activate only licensed modules. Each organization is a hard tenant boundary.

What is Trustity SecSend?

Trustity SecSend delivers sensitive files as sealed packages. Recipients unlock with a one-time SMS code rather than another shared password emailed in the same channel as the file. Putting the password in the same mailbox as the attachment is weak: a mailbox compromise yields both. An OTP on a second channel binds access to a factor the attacker may not have and reduces replay if only email is stolen.

How does HostGuard IPS work?

Trustity HostGuard IPS is host-based brute-force detection and blocking. It watches failed logons, can block offending source IPs at the endpoint firewall, and reports incidents to the Cloud Portal. Policy knobs include maximum login attempts, detection window, and ban duration. Start in Report only to learn normal helpdesk, jump-host, and automation noise before enforcement. A host-based approach to slowing RDP brute force is: detect failed-logon bursts, temporarily firewall the source, and alert SecOps in the portal. Helpdesk must be able to distinguish a HostGuard block from a generic outage.

Why rotate local admin passwords with PAM?

Trustity Vault / PAM combines a zero-knowledge vault with scheduled local administrator password rotation via the TAO agent. Unique, rotated local admin passwords limit lateral movement when a shared local admin secret is dumped, reduce the useful lifetime of stolen credentials, and pair with vaulting so operators retrieve a current secret instead of a static fleet password. Validate rotation only on a designated test asset so production accounts are not interrupted without approval.

Summarize VisionX visual-channel DLP for a security operator.

Trustity VisionX is camera-based / visual-channel DLP on the endpoint, enforced by the TAO agent. It detects phones, cameras, and lenses aimed at a screen, can capture evidence, and can lock the workstation when policy requires it. USB and email DLP do not see this path: a photo of the screen leaves the corporate digital perimeter. Compensating controls are detection plus a lock response (Faster / Balanced / More accurate in Cloud Portal policy) and operator review of VisionX live events. Model class labels today include phone and camera; dual detect (COCO plus Trustity VisionX weights) is the production confirmation path. Do not treat VisionX as a complete replacement for network DLP.

Summarize Pasting source code into public GenAI for a security operator.

Pasting source or secrets into a public GenAI chatbot is a data-loss path: content leaves the enterprise boundary, the vendor may retain or train on prompts depending on contract, and Shadow IT bypasses DLP that only inspects email, USB, or web-upload MIME types. Realistic leak paths for a SaaS team using ChatGPT daily include (1) paste of secrets and code into GenAI, (2) unsanctioned SaaS file uploads, (3) endpoint malware or a camera / shoulder-surf of the screen. Controls: browser DLP (GenGuard), approved enterprise GenAI with logging, secret scanning, and visual DLP (VisionX).
